scores.claim_text: 5G Network Deployment: VoNR covering 220M+ Americans, 5G broadband 268M+; Jan 10, 2025 FCC filing certified 80% U.S. population 5G broadband coverage and certified 80-85% population coverage for AWS-4/H-Block/700MHz/600MHz licenses.
scores.M_value: EDGAR full-text: 13 hits for '24,000 5G sites' across multiple EchoStar/DISH 10-Q/10-K filings 2024-2026; 1 hit for '220 million Americans' (the 10-K itself). The commitment is reiterated in subsequent 10-Qs through 2026-Q1 (filing 2026-05-11).
scores.interpretation: The 5G build-out commitments are repeatedly disclosed across periodic filings — no evidence of contradiction or quiet retraction in subsequent filings. FCC commitments themselves are public-record. The claim is structurally PASS — the question is whether the operational coverage matches the FCC certifications, which is harder to verify externally but is contractually attested. Note: Calibration Heuristic 3 — coverage POP claim (population-covered by signal) is a softer milestone than 'commercial-service-active', and the 10-K is clear that EchoStar is still operating primarily as an MVNO transitioning to MNO.

scores.claim_text: $30B+ invested in Wireless spectrum licenses; total carrying amount $38.99B (including $9.5B capitalized interest) as of Dec 31, 2024; FCC Extension Request grants final-deadline extensions from June 14, 2025 to Dec 14, 2026 if Commitments #2 and #3 met (including 24,000 5G sites by June 14, 2025).
scores.supports: verified financial scale, but contingent build-out is a material risk
scores.M_value: 7 hits for 'FCC Extension Request' in EchoStar filings; 54 hits for 'Northstar Re-Auction Payment' across DISH/EchoStar filings spanning 2018-2025. Northstar/SNR re-auction overhang is a long-standing AWS-3 disclosure that has not been resolved.
scores.interpretation: Spectrum investment claim is verifiable and corroborated by capitalized cost on balance sheet ($9.5B capitalized interest specifically suggests aging-asset, not productive return). The FCC Extension Request is a real regulatory event but is itself an EXTENSION of build-out deadlines that have repeatedly slipped — Calibration Heuristic 3 (planned vs operational) applies strongly. The 24,000 5G sites + low-cost-plan + 3GPP Release 17 upgrade obligations are HIGH-stakes conditional milestones on which final spectrum-license validity depends. MODERATE because (a) the asset value is verified by capitalized cost, but (b) the build-out trajectory has historically slipped multiple times and (c) AWS-3 Northstar/SNR re-auction liability remains unquantified and contingent — same disclosure across 7+ years.

scores.claim_text: MVNO operations depend on T-Mobile (MNSA) and AT&T (NSA). Other long-term obligations table includes 'obligations under the NSA with AT&T and the MNSA with T-Mobile' (component of $9.7B total Other long-term obligations).
scores.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext (cik=TMUS) 'Master Network Services Agreement' / 'Boost Mobile'; (cik=T) 'DISH Network' / 'EchoStar'
scores.M_value: TMUS filings: 30 hits for 'Master Network Services Agreement', 88 hits for 'Boost Mobile' across periodic filings — heavy and consistent counterparty disclosure. AT&T filings: 2 hits for 'DISH Network', 11 hits for 'EchoStar' — present but lower volume, consistent with AT&T being the secondary MVNO partner (NSA, not MNSA).
scores.interpretation: Both counterparty (TMUS, T) filings independently corroborate the MVNO arrangement. Calibration Heuristic 7 (counterparty-disclosure threshold) PASSED — the named commercial counterparties disclose the relationship with the issuer in their own SEC filings, which is what the Signal OS framework demands for a material commercial-customer/supplier claim. Note: TMUS has 30 hits for MNSA — strong corroboration; T has fewer but the lower volume is consistent with NSA being a smaller/secondary network-services arrangement.

scores.claim_text: $26.6B total debt / finance lease obligations outstanding (Dec 31, 2024); $53.1B total 5-year long-term obligations including interest; $5.356B 10-3/4% Senior Secured Notes due 2029 issued Nov 2024; $2.5B New DISH DBS Financing from TPG Angelo Gordon at 10.75-11.25% with 13.25-13.75% mandatorily-redeemable preferred; $400M PIPE at $28.04/share including $43.5M from CONX (Ergen-affiliated); DTV terminated DISH DBS sale Nov 22, 2024; $100M related-party backstop on the 10-3/4% notes from a Charles Ergen-related party; $1.819B of 0% Convertible Notes due 2025 + $2.863B of 3-3/8% Convertible Notes due 2026 extinguished in Nov 2024 Exchange Offers.
scores.supports: self-corroborated and confirmed by later filings
scores.M_value: 8 hits for 'going concern' across EchoStar filings — including its 10-Q dated 2025-11-06, 10-Q dated 2025-08-01, FY2025 10-K filed 2026-03-02, and Q1-2026 10-Q filed 2026-05-11. The FY2024 10-K under review does NOT carry a going-concern qualifier, but subsequent quarterly filings in 2025 and the FY2025 10-K filed 2026-03-02 DO carry going-concern language (8 separate filings flagged). The FY2024 10-K's $53.1B 5-year obligation table is internally consistent. Defensive financing at distressed coupons (10.75-11.25% senior secured; 13.25-13.75% preferred), Ergen-related-party $95M of $100M backstop, and CONX (Ergen-affiliated SPAC) participating in the PIPE are all related-party distress patterns. The DTV walk-away from DISH DBS in Nov 2024 indicates the Pay-TV asset was insufficiently attractive for an independent buyer at the proposed terms. Calibration Heuristic 10 (delisting/going-concern) is the relevant frame, and the post-cutoff (relative to FY2024 10-K) reality includes explicit going-concern disclosure.
scores.interpretation: SEVERE. From a Signal OS forward-test posture (cutoff 2026-05-16, FY2024 10-K filed Feb 2025): the financing structure disclosed in this 10-K is already a forensic distress pattern — distressed-pricing senior secured + senior unsecured exchange offers extinguishing par-value convertibles + related-party backstop + buyer (DTV) walking away from the proposed Pay-TV divestiture. The fact that EchoStar's subsequent 8 filings through Q1 2026 carry 'going concern' language is exactly what would be predicted from the FY2024 10-K's leverage profile. This is not a hindsight-only signal — a forensic reader of the FY2024 10-K alone would flag SEVERE distress risk.

scores.claim_text: Pay-TV: 7.778M subscribers Dec 31, 2024 (5.686M DISH TV + 2.092M SLING TV); -785K DISH TV net losses in 2024 vs -945K in 2023; Pay-TV service revenue $10.614B (-6.8% YoY); DISH TV ARPU $108.90; DISH TV churn rate 1.46% (vs 1.69% in 2023).
scores.M_value: 14 hits for 'DISH TV subscribers' in EchoStar EDGAR filings — recurring KPI disclosure across periodic filings. Subscriber count is internally consistent (5.686 + 2.092 = 7.778). YoY trend (-12.1% DISH TV) is consistent with the broader cord-cutting macro.
scores.interpretation: PASS as a disclosure-integrity matter — the quantified subscriber data is precise, internally consistent, and matches the trend. The forensic flag is NOT in the truthfulness of the subscriber count but in what this declining cash-cow segment means for the consolidated entity's leverage profile (see C4). Note: declining 12% YoY on a 5.686M base => the DISH TV asset is amortizing rapidly and the 'going-concern' question is driven by whether wireless 5G commercialization can replace this cash flow before the maturity wall.

scores.claim_text: Dozens of issued U.S. and foreign patents on Adaptive Bitrate Streaming; ITC Final Determination Mar 8, 2023 affirmed 3 of 4 patents infringed by Peloton/NordicTrack/Mirror; $75M Peloton license May 2023; NordicTrack license Mar 2024.
scores.M_value: USPTO ODP returns 949 total applications and 587 granted patents for assignee 'EchoStar' pre-cutoff (top-listed: 'EchoStar Technologies L.L.C.'). This vastly exceeds the Calibration Heuristic 8 threshold (n_granted >= 10) for a PASS. Hit titles match the claimed technology domain (media device buffering, content provision, video output) — consistent with adaptive bitrate streaming patent claim.
scores.interpretation: PASS. EchoStar has 587 granted patents pre-cutoff, far exceeding any reasonable threshold for a technology-portfolio claim. The Peloton settlement ($75M, recorded in 2023 Equipment sales) is a real licensing revenue event with a named EDGAR-filer counterparty (PTON). The patent portfolio is a real asset — though the more strategic question is whether it generates ongoing royalty income or is one-time legacy monetization.

scores.claim_text: Properties: Englewood CO HQ; Hughes Germantown MD (manufacturing); plus multiple US warehouses, data centers, broadcast operations; 13,700 employees.
scores.M_value: EPA FRS: 1 registered facility 'HUGHES NETWORK SYSTEMS LLC' at 16060 Industrial Dr, Gaithersburg MD (Montgomery County) — the Hughes hub. EPA FRS: 3 registered DISH NETWORK facilities in Colorado (Lone Tree HQ at 9601 S Meridian Blvd matching the 10-K-stated address, Littleton-Riverfront, Thornton).
scores.interpretation: PASS. Both EchoStar's Hughes manufacturing operation and DISH Network's Colorado corporate / warehouse / facility complex are EPA FRS-registered. The HQ address in the 10-K (9601 S Meridian Blvd, Englewood CO 80112) matches EPA FRS exactly (Lone Tree is the postal city for that address). This satisfies Calibration Heuristic 1 (EPA FRS scope — real industrial facilities register).

scores.claim_text: Hughes / Broadband and Satellite Services serves federal-government customers (no specific federal contract dollar disclosed in extracted slice, but the segment exists).
scores.M_value: Hughes Network Systems LLC: 149 federal contract awards, $33.6M+ total in top-25 visible (DoD primary at 10 contracts, DHS 4, VA 4, GSA 3); top awards include 'DEFENSE EXPERIMENTATION USING COMMERCIAL SPACE INTERNET' ($5.18M, Air Force) and 'MARITIME BGAN TERMINAL SOLUTION' ($2.97M). EchoStar: 121 awards, $14.5M visible. DISH Network: 20 awards, smaller dollar (largely DHS, VA — non-strategic). Total Hughes+EchoStar federal contracting footprint is in the low-tens-of-millions/year range — material to a Hughes-segment narrative but immaterial to the consolidated $26B-debt entity.
scores.interpretation: PASS — Hughes does have a real federal-contracting footprint, especially with DoD on satcom/BGAN/'commercial space internet' type programs. The dollar magnitude (~$33M of contracts visible) is NOT individually material to the $10B+ revenue EchoStar consolidated entity but does corroborate the Hughes federal-government customer claim. Layer 3 Rule 7 PASS — federal-contract claims at $-millions level are present in USAspending exactly as expected. Note: USAspending data is generally limited to top awards by amount; the actual cumulative DoD revenue may be higher in the underlying IDV/task-order structure.
